phenomenon: A hot thing left alone moves toward the temperature around it, fast at first and then slower. A radioactive sample does the same with the number of nuclei: the fraction left falls exponentially.
invariant: The fractional deviation from equilibrium decays in time with a single time constant; half-life = tau ln 2, independent of how large the deviation is.
operator: dx/dt = -(x - x_eq)/tau   (first order; tau is the time constant)
transfer: Radioactive decay: the half-life does not depend on how many nuclei you start with
Charge on a capacitor draining through a resistor
A temperature difference evening out
game_instance: A temperature difference, or a number of radioactive nuclei, shrinking by the same fraction in each time constant.
title: Linear relaxation

support.source: The Feynman Lectures on Physics, Volume I, Chapter 24 (Transients), and the exponential law of radioactive decay
support.note: The fraction left falls exponentially. The half-life does not depend on how large the start was.

phenomenon: Energy and charge do not appear or disappear. A level rises or falls only by the difference between what comes in and what goes out. If you cannot point to that difference, the account is not finished.
invariant: With no sources or sinks the total is conserved. To say there is less, you must point to where it went.
operator: d(rho)/dt + divergence of J = S   (continuity; S is the source or the sink)
transfer: Conservation of energy (Volume I, Chapter 4)
Conservation of charge
Heat leaving one body and entering another
game_instance: An energy account: what leaves one place has to enter another, or the books are wrong.
title: Conservation and flux

support.source: The Feynman Lectures on Physics, Volume I, Chapter 4, Conservation of Energy; Volume II, conservation of charge
support.note: If the books do not balance, you have not yet said where it went.

phenomenon: In a chain reaction each event can make more than one next event. The number then grows in proportion to the number already there, so the time to double stays the same for as long as that factor holds.
invariant: The doubling time is constant, t2 = ln(2)/k, while each generation is multiplied by the same factor.
operator: dx/dt = +k x    =>    x(t) = x0 exp(k t)    (k > 0)
transfer: A nuclear chain reaction with reproduction factor greater than one
Any growth that stays proportional to the amount already there, until a supply runs out
game_instance: Neutrons in a supercritical assembly: each generation larger than the last by the same factor.
title: Positive feedback and exponential growth

support.source: Surely You're Joking, Mr. Feynman!, the Los Alamos chapters, on a chain reaction; The Feynman Lectures on Physics, Volume I, the exponential when the growth rate is positive
support.note: While each event makes more than one next event, the doubling time stays put.

phenomenon: A free oscillator with friction does not ring forever. Light friction: it swings, and the swings shrink. Heavy friction: it creeps back and does not swing. In between, it returns about as fast as it can without swinging past rest.
invariant: Disturbances die out. The damping ratio separates underdamped, critically damped, and overdamped motion.
operator: x double-dot + 2 zeta omega x-dot + omega^2 x = 0
transfer: Volume I, Chapter 24, the damped transient
A circuit with resistance, inductance, and capacitance
game_instance: A mass on a spring in a thin liquid, or in a thick one.
title: Negative feedback and damping

support.source: The Feynman Lectures on Physics, Volume I, Chapter 24, Transients
support.note: Friction on an oscillator gives three regimes: ringing that shrinks, a creep with no swing, and the border between them.

phenomenon: A ferromagnet can keep a magnetization after the outside field is taken away. To come back you need a field the other way. Crossing that point puts the material in a different state.
invariant: Past a critical field the material sits in another state, and returning takes a different condition. That is hysteresis.
operator: Two states separated by a barrier: the system stays in one until the barrier is crossed.
transfer: Volume II, ferromagnetism and the hysteresis loop
A chain reaction below and above criticality, where the behavior changes at one value
game_instance: Magnetizing a piece of iron, then reversing the field to bring it back.
title: Thresholds and bifurcation

support.source: The Feynman Lectures on Physics, Volume II, ferromagnetism and hysteresis
support.note: The way back is not the way you came: a reversed field is needed to undo the magnetization.

phenomenon: A little extra gas let into one corner of a box spreads until it is even. It does not keep piling up. The difference that drives the flow shrinks, and there is a final even state.
invariant: There is a final uniform concentration. The flow slows as the difference that drives it gets smaller.
operator: The diffusion equation carries a lump toward a uniform concentration. The uniform state has no further flow.
transfer: Volume I, Chapter 43: a special gas spreading through a background gas
A temperature difference evening out in the same way
game_instance: A trace of gas, or a drop of dye in still water, spreading until the container is uniform.
title: Saturation and capacity

support.source: The Feynman Lectures on Physics, Volume I, Chapter 43, Diffusion
support.note: Nearby teaching of the same kind: a driven difference dies out at a final even state, rather than a logistic population curve, which is not this lecture.

phenomenon: An oscillator has a frequency of its own. Drive it near that frequency and the amplitude grows. Push a swing at the period it already has, and each push adds.
invariant: There is a natural frequency. The response is largest when the drive is near that frequency.
operator: Driven oscillator: the amplitude peaks near the natural frequency; the sharpness is the quality factor.
transfer: Volume I, Chapter 23, resonance
An electrical resonant circuit
game_instance: A swing, or a mass on a spring, driven at its own period.
title: Oscillation and resonance

support.source: The Feynman Lectures on Physics, Volume I, Chapter 23, Resonance
support.note: Drive near the natural frequency and the amplitude is largest.

phenomenon: A small amount of a different gas, put in one place in a box, spreads because the molecules are knocked about at random. The mean square distance from the start grows in proportion to the time.
invariant: Mean square displacement is proportional to t. The distance that matters grows like the square root of the time.
operator: partial c / partial t = D times the laplacian of c
transfer: Volume I, Chapter 41: mean square distance proportional to time
Volume I, Chapter 43: diffusion of a special gas
game_instance: A grain of dye in still water, or a trace of gas released in one corner of a box.
title: Diffusion and random walks

support.source: The Feynman Lectures on Physics, Volume I, Chapter 41 (The Brownian Movement) and Chapter 43 (Diffusion)
support.note: The mean square distance grows in proportion to the time, not to the square of the time.

phenomenon: A chain of events dies out if each event makes, on average, fewer than one successor. It runs away if each event makes more than one. There is a critical point between dying out and spreading.
invariant: The critical value is a mean number of successors equal to one. Below it the chain dies. Above it a large chain appears.
operator: Branching mean k: k < 1 dies out, k = 1 is critical, k > 1 grows.
transfer: A nuclear chain reaction below and above criticality
Exponential growth in Volume I when the growth rate is positive
game_instance: Neutrons in an assembly: losses against new neutrons from fission.
title: Critical branching

support.source: Surely You're Joking, Mr. Feynman!, the Los Alamos chapters (critical assemblies); The Feynman Lectures on Physics, Volume I, exponential growth when the rate is positive
support.note: The lattice-percolation formula is not this lecture. The nearby teaching of the same kind is a chain that dies out or runs, split by a critical reproduction factor.

phenomenon: A ratchet and pawl with both sides at the same temperature does not turn steadily one way. When one side is hotter, a one-way motion can run, and the heat does not come back by itself.
invariant: A one-way process does not reverse itself while the two temperatures are equal. Getting the energy back takes a difference.
operator: At equal temperatures the forward and backward rates match, so there is no steady one-way motion.
transfer: Volume I, Chapter 46, the ratchet and pawl
A log that burns does not reassemble itself from the gases and the heat
game_instance: A ratchet that will not steadily lift a weight when both sides are at the same temperature.
title: Irreversibility

support.source: The Feynman Lectures on Physics, Volume I, Chapter 46, Ratchet and pawl
support.note: At one temperature the ratchet does not run one way and stay run. The Markov-chain formula is not this lecture.

phenomenon: The electric charge you measure depends on the scale at which you look. A number that looked constant at one resolution is a different number at another. The rule stays; the parameter runs.
invariant: A coupling can change with the scale. At a fixed point it stops running, and the behavior looks the same at every scale you still resolve.
operator: Integrate out the short-distance detail and keep a coupling that depends on the scale you still resolve.
transfer: Quantum electrodynamics: the charge depending on the momentum scale
The Nobel lecture of 1965, on how renormalization was built
game_instance: The electron's charge, compared at two different resolutions.
title: Renormalization and scale migration

support.source: Richard P. Feynman, Nobel lecture, 1965, on the development of quantum electrodynamics and renormalization
support.note: The coastline picture is not his. The scale idea he did teach is that the charge you measure depends on the resolution.

phenomenon: You can add a gradient to the vector potential and the electric and magnetic fields do not change. Two different potentials can be the same physics. The zero of the electrostatic potential is a choice of the same kind.
invariant: What you measure is unchanged by that shift. The physics is the class of potentials that give the same fields, not one written choice.
operator: A_mu goes to A_mu plus the gradient of chi, and the fields stay the same.
transfer: Volume II, the vector potential and the freedom to add a gradient
The arbitrary zero of electrostatic potential
game_instance: Two gauges of one and the same electromagnetic field.
title: Gauge redundancy and invariants

support.source: The Feynman Lectures on Physics, Volume II, the vector potential
support.note: Adding a gradient to the potential leaves the electric and magnetic fields unchanged.
